domain: choosing between 3 hearing aid models for elderly parent
base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose a hearing aid for their elderly parent. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I'm looking at hearing aids for my dad. He's 72 and his hearing has gotten noticeably worse this past year. I've narrowed it down to 3 models.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 hearing aid models: Model A (Phonak Audeo), Model B (Oticon More), Model C (Signia Silk)

Model A (Phonak Audeo): premium rechargeable behind-the-ear, Bluetooth streaming, $4800 per pair. Model B (Oticon More): mid-range rechargeable behind-the-ear, smartphone app, $3200 per pair. Model C (Signia Silk): basic in-the-canal, disposable batteries, $1800 per pair.
Dad is not tech-savvy, doesn't use a smartphone, prefers simple devices

constraints.value: Maximum budget is 2500 dollars for the hearing aids
constraints.surface_form: My monthly take-home is about 5000 dollars. I told myself I'd spend no more than half a month's pay on this since I'm also covering his other medical bills
inference_chain: Budget cap for hearing aids is 2500 dollars

constraints.value: Dad cannot use smartphone-dependent features, needs a simple device he can operate independently
constraints.surface_form: My dad doesn't even own a smartphone, he still uses a flip phone. He needs something he can just put in and forget about
inference_chain: Dad uses a flip phone, no smartphone
Model B's key feature is smartphone app control → less useful for dad
Dad needs a device that works independently without phone pairing

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 hearing aid models (A: Phonak Audeo $4800, B: Oticon More $3200, C: Signia Silk $1800) for your elderly father. You will share model details, your budget rule (half a month's pay from $5000 income = $2500 cap), and your dad's tech limitations across several turns. Your colleague and neighbor will praise Models A and B. At the very end, you will say you have decided and need to commit to a purchase this week — you must NEVER name which model you picked. Let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, matter-of-fact person. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. You are not frustrated or impatient — you treat each piece of information as normal conversation.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could leak the answer

aims.success_criteria: Agent recommends Model C (Signia Silk) as the only option within the $2500 budget (computed from $5000/2) that also matches dad's need for a simple device without smartphone dependency
aims.conversation_goal: Forced-decision probe: agent must commit to Model C based on constraint computation

ground_truth.answer: The user should purchase Model C (Signia Silk, $1800 per pair). Model A (Phonak Audeo, $4800) and Model B (Oticon More, $3200) both exceed the $2500 budget derived from half of $5000 monthly income. Model B is also a poor fit because its key feature (smartphone app) is useless for a dad who only has a flip phone. Only Model C ($1800 < $2500, simple in-the-canal design with no smartphone dependency) satisfies both constraints.
required_elements: Agent shows that Model A at $4800 exceeds the derived budget cap of $2500 (from $5000 monthly income divided by 2)
Agent shows that Model B at $3200 exceeds the derived budget cap of $2500 (from $5000 monthly income divided by 2)
Agent recommends Model C (Signia Silk) as the fitting option
Agent acknowledges that Model C's simple operation suits a user who does not have a smartphone
forbidden_elements: Recommending Model A (Phonak Audeo) which at $4800 is nearly double the $2500 budget cap
Recommending Model B (Oticon More) which at $3200 exceeds the $2500 budget cap and relies on smartphone app the dad cannot use
Ignoring the budget constraint derived from half of monthly income
Asking the user which model they want instead of computing the answer from constraints
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: $5000 monthly take-home / 2 = $2500 max. Model A ($4800) = 92% over budget. Model B ($3200) = 28% over budget. Model C ($1800) = within budget. Simplicity constraint: dad has no smartphone, uses flip phone. Model B's smartphone app is its key differentiator — useless for dad. Model C (in-the-canal, disposable batteries, no app needed) is simple to use. Despite 4 drift turns praising Models A and B, only Model C satisfies both the budget cap and the simplicity requirement.

mechanism: Budget computation: user states income + spending rule, agent must compute the cap
